paragraph: If you are training for a 5 km run (3.11 miles), maintaining a pace of 6 minutes per kilometre (9.66 minutes per mile) means you will finish in approximately 30 minutes (0.5 hours). A beginner might start with 2 km (1.24 miles) of running and gradually increase the distance by 0.5 km (0.31 miles) each week. Drinking 500 mL (16.91 US fluid ounces) of water before exercise can help you stay hydrated.

In science class, you might measure the temperature of water at 25°C (77°F) before conducting an experiment. If you heat 500 mL (16.91 US fluid ounces) of water to 100°C (212°F), it reaches its boiling point at standard atmospheric pressure. A laboratory ruler can measure an object's length as 15 cm (5.91 inches), while a balance might record its mass as 250 g (8.82 ounces).

When shipping a package, its dimensions and weight are often required to calculate the delivery cost. A box measuring 40 cm (15.75 inches) long, 30 cm (11.81 inches) wide, and 20 cm (7.87 inches) tall has a volume of 24,000 cm³ (1,464.57 cubic inches). If the package weighs 5 kg (11.02 pounds), the shipping company may charge based on its actual weight or dimensional weight. Checking both metric and imperial measurements helps prevent shipping delays.

During air travel, passengers often see their cruising altitude displayed in feet and metres. A commercial aircraft flying at 35,000 ft (10,668 m) is travelling at a typical cruising altitude. If the aircraft covers 800 km (497.10 miles) in 1 hour, its average ground speed is 800 km/h (497.10 mph). Airport baggage allowances may also specify a maximum checked-bag weight of 23 kg (50.71 pounds).

When planning a garden, knowing the correct measurements helps determine how much soil and water you need. A garden bed measuring 2 m (6.56 ft) long and 1.5 m (4.92 ft) wide has an area of 3 m² (32.29 square feet). Adding a 5 cm (1.97 inches) layer of compost requires approximately 0.15 m³ (5.30 cubic feet) of material. Many vegetables also benefit from approximately 25 mm (0.98 inches) of water per week, depending on rainfall and soil conditions.

Home heating systems are commonly measured by their energy output and the temperature they maintain indoors. Setting a thermostat to 20°C (68°F) can provide a comfortable indoor environment during winter. A room measuring 5 m (16.40 ft) long, 4 m (13.12 ft) wide, and 2.5 m (8.20 ft) high has a volume of 50 m³ (1,765.73 cubic feet). Insulation rated at R-20 (RSI 3.52 m²·K/W) offers a useful measure of resistance to heat flow.

When calculating car fuel consumption, it is useful to understand both litres per 100 kilometres and miles per gallon. A vehicle that consumes 8 L/100 km (29.4 US mpg) uses 8 litres of fuel (2.11 US gallons) to travel 100 km (62.14 miles). If a car has a 50 L (13.21 US gallon) fuel tank, it can travel approximately 625 km (388.36 miles) under those consumption conditions. Actual fuel economy can vary depending on traffic, speed, and driving habits.

A cyclist training for a long-distance event might ride 25 km (15.53 miles) in approximately 1 hour. This corresponds to an average speed of 25 km/h (15.53 mph). If the cyclist drinks 750 mL (25.36 US fluid ounces) of water during the ride, that is approximately 0.75 L (0.20 US gallons). Wearing a helmet weighing 300 g (10.58 ounces) can provide protection without adding excessive weight.

In a chemistry experiment, a student might need to measure 2.5 L (0.66 US gallons) of liquid for a reaction. If the liquid has a density of 1 g/mL (1 kg/L), its total mass is 2.5 kg (5.51 pounds). A thermometer showing 37°C (98.6°F) indicates a temperature close to normal human body temperature. Measuring 10 mL (0.34 US fluid ounces) with a graduated cylinder provides a more precise result than estimating the amount by eye.

When heating a home, energy consumption may be measured in kilowatt-hours and British thermal units. Using 10 kWh (34,121.4 BTU) of energy provides the same energy quantity in either unit. A 2 kW (6,824 BTU/h) electric heater operating for 5 hours (300 minutes) consumes 10 kWh (34,121.4 BTU) of electricity. If electricity costs $0.15 per kWh (approximately $0.044 per 1,000 BTU), the total operating cost is $1.50 (150 cents).
